register: The services a persona can hold a credential for, and what each needs
note: QGD-PSN-0002 and QGD-PSN-0003. This is the only place a service is named. The setup screens, the command validation and the per-service test all read it, so a service added here appears with its own fields and its own test and no code change — the rule QGD-REF-0005 applies to ADIF's definitions, applied to services. The credential core names no service at all: it treats a provider as an identifier and stores whatever it is given (QGD-CRD-0003), so there is no second list in Rust for this one to drift from.

fieldKinds.username: An account name, which is not a secret and is shown
fieldKinds.password: A secret, never shown and never logged
fieldKinds.api_key: A secret of the service's own issuing, never shown and never logged

services.name: QRZ.com
services.what: Callsign lookup — who a callsign belongs to, and where
services.howToGet: A QRZ account. Lookup by callsign needs an XML subscription; the account alone will be refused by the lookup service.

test.what: Asks QRZ for a session with the username and password, and nothing else

services.name: QRZ Logbook
services.what: QRZ's logbook — uploading and fetching QSOs
services.howToGet: The logbook's own API key, from the logbook's settings. It is not the QRZ account password, and a logbook has one key per book.

test.what: Asks the logbook for its status with the key, which returns the book's name and QSO count

services.name: eQSL.cc
services.what: Electronic QSL cards — the inbox, and whether a station is Authenticity Guaranteed
services.howToGet: An eQSL account. The callsign the account is registered under has to be the persona's.

test.what: Asks eQSL to verify the account, which answers without returning any card

services.name: Logbook of The World
services.what: ARRL's confirmation service — QSOs and the credits they count towards
services.howToGet: An ARRL LoTW account, and a certificate ARRL issues after checking the licence. The certificate is a PKCS#12 file with a date in it and has to be renewed.

expires.what: ARRL's certificate carries its own expiry, which the credential core reads from the certificate rather than asking the operator to remember it (QGD-PSN-0006)

test.what: Asks LoTW for the account's own QSO count, which needs the username and password and returns no QSO

services.name: HamQTH
services.what: Callsign lookup, free — a second opinion to QRZ's
services.howToGet: A free HamQTH account. Most of HamQTH answers without one; lookup does not.

test.what: Asks HamQTH for a session key, which it returns or refuses

services.name: Club Log
services.howToGet: A Club Log account, and an API key the operator asks Club Log for. Both are needed: the key identifies the application and the account identifies the operator.

test.what: Asks Club Log to check the account, which answers yes or no and returns no log
